lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday FM. The news is reassuringly over.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: You're listening to Yesterday FM, broadcasting from twenty four hours ago. Nothing left to worry about.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday FM. It's already happened. You liked it.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday FM, one hundred point eight five. Everything turned out fine.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: More or less.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Good morning, yesterday. This is Yesterday Morning. Breakfast has been eaten. The dishes are done.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday morning's top story: you woke up.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Well done. Everything after that was a bonus.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: This is The Afternoon Before. The light's gone gold. It stays gold. It's already stayed gold. Put your feet up.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A little traffic from yesterday afternoon. The school run went well. Everybody had their bag. One child had two bags.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: We don't know whose the other bag was. It's being looked into. Gently.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Good evening. This is Last Night, Tonight. We'll go through it together. Don't worry. I know how it ends.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Last night, at about two in the morning, the operator on the relay ship Nightjar was still at the console, with the kettle on.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: They made it through the shift. I know. I've read the log. Well done, you.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Four in the morning, last night. Everything very still. Somebody, somewhere, couldn't sleep.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Then, at about half past, they could. That might have been you. It went fine.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Here's the news. It's yesterday's. Don't worry. It's over.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The headlines, from yesterday. Settle in. Everything turned out fine, more or less.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: At the third pip, it was yesterday. Here's the news.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A man on Pell Street was worried about a meeting yesterday. The meeting happened. It was eleven minutes long. Nobody mentioned the thing he was worried about.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: He's forgotten it already. So, in a way, have we.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: It nearly rained yesterday. It looked like it was going to, all afternoon. Several people took coats.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: In the end, it didn't. The coats have been informed.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday's big story: a missing Tuesday was found in a ditch outside Precinct Nine. That's old news now, which is the best kind of news.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The Tuesday is recovering at home, and is expected to go ahead next week as planned.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A cat got stuck up a tree yesterday afternoon. A crowd gathered. The fire brigade was called.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Then the cat came down by itself, as cats do, and walked off as though nothing had happened. Nothing had.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Sport. There was a match yesterday. Somebody won.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The other side played very well, considering, and everybody shook hands and went home for their tea.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A letter was posted yesterday that someone had been putting off for months. It said what it needed to say.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The reply came this morning. It said: thank you for writing. That was all. That was enough.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The markets went up yesterday, and then down, and then closed, as they do.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Nobody lost anything they haven't since found down the back of a sofa.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A kettle was put on yesterday at four, and again at half past, and once more just after six. All three cups of tea were drunk.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: One of them went cold first. It has been forgiven.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: And yesterday's weather: mild, then evening. You were there for most of it.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: That was the news. All of it has happened. None of it can happen again. Rest easy.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday's weather: a bright start, some cloud after lunch, and a lovely sunset nobody quite stopped to look at. It's on again tonight. Do stop.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: That was yesterday. It went fine. Most days do, in the end.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday's weather, in full. The morning was grey, and then it made up its mind. Light winds from the west, which is where they'd been heading all along.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: In the afternoon, a cloud shaped like a dog went over Pell Street. Then it was evening, and then it was night, and then it was today.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: And here we are.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday's traffic and travel. All the roads went where they were going. There was a hold-up on the ring road at about five, and then there wasn't.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Everyone got home. Some of them stopped for chips on the way. Good for them.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: That was a song from yesterday. You liked it then. You'll like it now.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: It isn't going anywhere. That's the lovely thing about yesterday.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The calendar on the wall still says yesterday. Somebody asked if I'd like to tear the page off.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: I said, what for? It was a good day. Let's leave it up a bit.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: My tea's gone cold. It went cold yesterday. That's the kind of tea it is.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: I drink it anyway. Cold tea is only tea that waited for you.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The clock on the wall runs gently backwards. Some people find that upsetting.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: I find it reassuring. Every tick, there's a little less to worry about.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday FM. You're on the air.

lines.speaker: Maggie, Worried About Tomorrow
lines.text: Gordon, I've got a big day tomorrow, and I'm worried.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: I can't tell you about tomorrow, I'm afraid. I'm only licensed for yesterday.

lines.speaker: Maggie, Worried About Tomorrow
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: But I can tell you about yesterday. Yesterday, you were worried about today. And here you are, today, on the phone to the radio, making plans. You got through it.

lines.speaker: Maggie, Worried About Tomorrow
lines.text: I suppose I did.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Ring me the day after tomorrow. I'll tell you how it went.

lines.speaker: Maggie, Worried About Tomorrow
lines.text: All right, Gordon. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: A note from yesterday. Halloween is coming, I'm told. I can't see it from here.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: But I can tell you about last year's. Everyone got home. All the sweets were eaten. The ghosts were mostly children, and the one that wasn't was very polite.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: It's Halloween for you today. Here, it's still the thirtieth. Everyone's carving pumpkins. Somebody lost a cat costume, and found it again, on the cat.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: It's all going to be fine. I'll tell you tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: Yesterday was Halloween. It went fine. Every pumpkin was carved, and every door was knocked.

lines.speaker: Gordon Ago
lines.text: The sweets ran out at nine, as they always do, and everybody pretended they were all right about it. Nobody was frightened for long.
